intro: What engineering must implement and test before go-live to stop account discovery, brute force, request forgery, privilege escalation and data leaking through API responses. Mapped to OWASP ASVS 4.0.3 (Level 2) and the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023).

coreRule.heading: Core rule: the browser is untrusted
coreRule.body: Everything in a request (user ID, email, role, tenant, price, status, hidden fields) can be edited in DevTools or a proxy. The server works out who the caller is from the session cookie alone, loads their role and tenant from its own database, and checks permission on every request and every record. Hiding a button in the UI is not a control.

neverSend: Internal or sequential user, tenant or record IDs (use random, non-guessable IDs where an ID is needed)
Roles, permissions or tenant IDs that the server later trusts
Password hashes, MFA secrets, recovery codes, reset tokens
Session or access tokens in the body, URL or localStorage
Failed-attempt counters, lock status or "account exists" flags
Other users’ emails, phone numbers or IPs beyond what the role is allowed to see
Stack traces, SQL errors, file paths, framework or server versions
Fields the screen does not display (no "select *" serialisation)
badResponse:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: [server name and version]
X-Powered-By: [framework name]

{
  "user": {
    "id": "[sequential internal id]",
    "email": "[user email]",
    "role": "[role the server later trusts]",
    "tenant_id": "[internal tenant id]",
    "password_hash": "[hash]",
    "mfa_secret": "[secret]",
    "failed_attempts": "[counter]",
    "locked": "[flag]"
  },
  "token": "[bearer token in body, saved to localStorage]"
}
goodResponse:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: no-store
Set-Cookie: __Host-mfa_pending=[opaque]; Max-Age=300; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/

{
  "next": "mfa"
}

groups.title: Server-side identity and authorisation
groups.threat: Changing a user_id, policy_id or tenant_id in a request to read or change another person’s or company’s data, or sending role=admin to gain rights (IDOR, privilege escalation).
controls: Identity comes only from the server-side session; user_id, email, role or tenant sent by the client is ignored
Every query is scoped by the session’s tenant (row-level security in the database as a second layer)
Object-level check on every read and write: does this user have this right on this record?
Function-level check on every admin endpoint; deny by default
Allow-list of writable fields per endpoint; role, owner, tenant and status are never bindable from the body (mass assignment)
Policy edits verified against owner_id = session user on the server, not by hiding the button
groups.refs: ASVS V4 (Access control) · API1 BOLA, API3 property-level authorisation, API5 function-level authorisation
groups.test: Automated cross-tenant and cross-user tests with two accounts swapping IDs on every endpoint

groups.title: Account discovery (enumeration)
groups.threat: Trying emails on sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password or invite screens to learn which accounts exist, then targeting them.
controls: Same status code, body and response time for existing and non-existing emails on login, sign-up, forgot-password and MFA
Dummy password hash computed for unknown emails so timing matches
Sign-up always answers "check your inbox"; an existing user gets a different email, not a different screen
Lockout applies to any email string, so locking does not reveal real accounts
No public user search, profile URLs or autocomplete of emails before sign-in
Invite and reset links carry only an opaque token, never an email or user ID
groups.refs: ASVS V2.2 (General authenticator security), V2.5 (Credential recovery) · API2 Broken authentication
groups.test: Compare responses and timing for real vs unknown emails (100 runs each); differences must be within noise

groups.title: Brute force and credential stuffing
groups.threat: Guessing passwords or MFA codes for a known email, or testing leaked email/password pairs from other breaches.
controls: Per-email, per-IP and per-device limits with growing delays (see table below)
Bot check from the 3rd failure; WAF bot management at the edge
Detect many emails from one IP or many IPs on one email; block and alert
Breached/common-password check at sign-up and password change (min 12, up to 128 characters, no composition rules)
MFA required for every account, so a correct password alone is not enough
MFA codes: single use, 30-second window, 5 attempts per sign-in
Owner alerted by email after repeated failures or a new-device sign-in
groups.refs: ASVS V2.2.1, V2.1.7, V2.8 (One-time verifiers) · API2, API4 Unrestricted resource consumption
groups.test: Scripted brute-force and stuffing runs in staging; confirm throttling, alerts and no bypass via alternate endpoints (mobile API, legacy routes)

groups.title: Password reset and account recovery
groups.threat: Resetting someone else’s password by guessing or reusing a token, changing the email in the request, or poisoning the reset link.
controls: Token: 256-bit random, stored only as a hash, single use, 15-minute expiry, bound to one account
The server finds the account from the token; any email or user_id in the reset request is ignored
New request or successful reset invalidates all older tokens
Reset link built from a fixed base URL, never from the Host header
Reset revokes all sessions and still requires MFA; the owner is notified
Admins can only send a reset link to the member’s verified email; they never see or set passwords
MFA reset: identity check plus second approver; audited
groups.test: Token reuse, expiry, swap-user, Host-header injection and parallel-request (race) tests

groups.title: Sessions, tokens and request forgery
groups.threat: Stealing or fixing a session, or making a signed-in user’s browser send an unwanted request (CSRF).
controls: Session in a cookie with __Host- prefix, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict; opaque and server-side revocable
New session ID after sign-in, MFA and any role change
Idle and absolute timeouts; sign-out and password change kill all sessions
CSRF token on every state-changing request, plus Origin/Referer checks
Re-authentication (password + MFA) for sensitive actions: change email, reset another user’s MFA, export data, change billing
No tokens in URLs, logs or browser storage
groups.test: Session fixation, CSRF on every POST/PUT/DELETE, cookie flag scan, logout invalidation

groups.title: Data minimisation in API responses
groups.threat: Reading sensitive fields from DevTools or a proxy that the screen never shows.
controls: Response DTOs per endpoint with explicit field lists; no direct serialisation of database models
Masking by role (e.g. members see colleagues’ names, not emails or IPs)
Random UUIDs instead of sequential IDs where an ID must be exposed
Cache-Control: no-store on all authenticated and auth responses
No sensitive data in query strings, error messages or analytics events
groups.test: Schema review of every response against the screen’s needs; automated check for forbidden field names

groups.title: Input handling
groups.threat: Injection, oversized payloads or unexpected types used to break the server or bypass checks.
controls: Strict schema validation on every request (type, length, format; unknown fields rejected)
Parameterised queries and ORM only; no string-built SQL
Output encoding and Content-Security-Policy against XSS in policies and comments
File uploads: type checked by content, size limit, malware scan, stored outside the web root
Request size and pagination limits
groups.refs: ASVS V5 (Validation, sanitisation, encoding), V12 (Files) · API4, API8
groups.test: DAST in CI plus manual injection testing of rich-text and upload fields

groups.title: Errors, headers and transport
groups.threat: Learning the technology stack or internals from error pages and headers.
controls: Generic error messages with a reference ID; details only in server logs
Remove Server, X-Powered-By and version headers
HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame-ancestors none, Referrer-Policy strict-origin
TLS 1.2+ only; CORS limited to the app’s own origin, no wildcards with credentials
No debug endpoints, API explorers or source maps in production
groups.refs: ASVS V7.4 (Error handling), V9 (Communications), V14 (Configuration) · API8 Security misconfiguration
groups.test: Header scan, forced-error testing, TLS configuration scan

groups.title: Logging, monitoring and alerting
groups.threat: Attacks going unnoticed, or logs themselves leaking secrets.
controls: Log every sign-in, failure, lock, reset, MFA change, role change and admin action with actor, tenant, IP and result
Never log passwords, tokens, MFA codes or full request bodies on auth routes
Hash-chained, write-once audit store; streamed to the SIEM
Alerts: failure spikes, stuffing patterns, impossible travel, admin actions outside hours, cross-tenant access denials
Users see their own sign-in history and active sessions
groups.refs: ASVS V7.1–V7.3 (Logging) · ISO 27001 A.8.15–A.8.16 · SOC 2 CC7.2
groups.test: Replay attack scenarios and confirm the alert fires within the agreed time

rateLimitsIntro: Limits are keyed on the identifier string the caller sends, not on whether an account exists, so unknown emails behave exactly like real ones. Tune from monitoring after launch.

rateLimits.id: 5 failures per 15 min, then 15-min pause; bot check from the 3rd
rateLimits.ip: 20 per min; more than 50 distinct emails per hour blocks the IP
rateLimits.then: 429 with the same body for every email; owner alerted if the account exists
Pending sign-in cancelled; password step must restart after the wait
Request dropped quietly; response is still 202 "accepted"
Token voided; user must request a new link
429; exports limited to 10 per hour and always logged

matrixIntro: Checked in the API on every request. The tenant always comes from the session, so no role can reach another company's records. Deny by default; any action not listed is refused.
releaseGate: Penetration test of the web app and API by an independent firm; all critical and high findings fixed and retested
OWASP ASVS Level 2 self-assessment completed and signed off by the CISO
Automated cross-tenant / cross-user (IDOR) test suite passing in CI
Enumeration timing test: no measurable difference between real and unknown emails
Rate limits and alerts demonstrated in staging with scripted attacks
Response schema review: no forbidden fields in any API response
Security headers, TLS and cookie flags verified by scan
Secrets in a vault; no keys in code, images or front-end bundles
